quickSummary: Non-cyclic photophosphorylation connects PS II (P680) and PS I (P700) along a redox potential gradient (the Z-Scheme). The luminal Oxygen Evolving Complex (Mn4CaO5 cluster) splits 2 H2O into 4 H+ (in lumen), 4 electrons, and 1 O2 across the Kok S-state cycle. Excited electrons flow: P680 -> Pheophytin -> Plastoquinone -> Cytochrome b6f (pumps 8 H+ via Q-cycle) -> Plastocyanin -> P700 -> A0/A1 -> Fx -> FA/FB -> Ferredoxin -> FNR -> NADPH + H+.

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
NON-CYCLIC ELECTRON PATHWAY
                      
   2 H₂O ──► [OEC (Mn₄CaO₅)] ──► Y_Z ──► P680 ──► Pheophytin ──► Plastoquinone (PQ_A ──► PQ_B)
                                                                       │

       │
       ▼
   A₀ (Chl) ──► A₁ (Phylloquinone) ──► F_X ──► F_A/F_B ──► Ferredoxin (Fd) ──► FNR ──► NADP⁺
conceptBreakdown.content:
1. **Oxygen Evolving Complex (OEC)**: Located on the **LUMINAL side** of the thylakoid membrane, bound to PS II. Contains a **$\text{Mn}_4\text{CaO}_5$ cluster** cycling through 5 oxidation states ($S_0\text{--}S_4$ Kok cycle) to split water:
   $$2\text{H}_2\text{O} \xrightarrow[\text{Tyrosine}_Z]{\text{OEC / }\text{Mn}_4\text{CaO}_5} 4\text{H}^+\text{ (Lumen)} + 4\text{e}^- + \text{O}_2\uparrow$$
2. **Plastoquinone Pool (PQ)**: Mobile lipid-soluble quinone that picks up $2\text{e}^-$ from PS II and $2\text{H}^+$ from stroma, transferring electrons to Cytochrome $b_6f$ while pumping protons into the lumen via the Q-cycle.
3. **Plastocyanin (PC)**: Soluble, copper-containing luminal protein delivering electrons to $\text{P700}^+$ (PS I).
4. **Ferredoxin-NADP+ Reductase (FNR)**: Stroma-facing flavoenzyme with an FAD cofactor catalyzing:
   $$\text{NADP}^+ + 2\text{H}^+\text{ (Stroma)} + 2\text{e}^- \xrightarrow{\text{FNR}} \text{NADPH} + \text{H}^+$$
